paragraphs: By the way, I built a rather entertaining mechanism that does delightful things:
1) It shows what I have in subscriptions in general, and what the status is where. Well, that's elementary.
2) It also stores sessions regardless of the type of login available (whether OAuth OpenAI / Claude or the subscription API of Kimi / Qwen)
And both on the computer and on the server.
3) It also determines where it's best to do a given task — on the computer or on the server — and in any case will do it on the server if the computer isn't available.
4) For low-risk tasks it also picks the most depleted subscription by the criterion “depletion + update deadline,” so as to scrape every available subscription down to zero.
But for high-risk tasks (for example SLSBMB.com tasks or some others) it picks, on the contrary, the least depleted subscription of the needed type regardless of the limit-reset deadline).

5) When a subscription hits 1%, it also launches a Kimi session with fallback to Qwen with fallback to Codex, so that the session studies which sessions are currently running on the dying subscription, what their purpose is and how to correctly shut them down and relaunch them on a fresh subscription via resume without harm to the task, and even so that the task doesn't notice anything happened at all. It does this shutdown and relaunch in a new window, closes the old windows and closes its own window, switching itself off when the task is successfully completed. All of this is accompanied by notifications I can't fail to read, because the icon blinks in the tray.

6) It also manages my smart Telegram bot gate, which now determines from what I said into Telegram or the watch exactly what I need and where it's best to do it, with which subscription, and launches the process, all in fractions of a second.

And I can separately say, like, do it on the server — and then it won't think about where to do it but will hand it precisely to a server session. If I said which — precisely that one. If I didn't say — it'll pick itself.

7) Having bought a new key, I can simply say in Telegram, we have a new subscription, the token is copied to the clipboard, please connect it to our whole … according to the instructions, “this is Kimi,” or “this is Qwen,” and it'll connect it, assigning the next number.
8) And of course once an hour it checks the CLIs for available upgrades and upgrades them seamlessly.
Convenient as …. On the whole I no longer have to think about juggling subscriptions in any position of the body or state of mind. Everything happens by itself:*****

There's a lot more there of course; for example I can look at where which sessions are currently active, how long they've been running, how many tokens they've burned, when they last emitted log growth, etc.
I'm cracking up at curly-haired Dario Amadeus. … he says, they distilled us; that's the only reason anyone else has AI. We're descendants of aliens, and all of them — aren't.

I'm just curious: if the Chinese and everyone else … more than 2.5 million models and other AI creations unconnected with Anthropic onto Hugging Face by the start of 2026, can there really not be another two or three teams in the world capable of making their own models? Is that even conceivable?

Is 5.6 Sol by any chance a distillate of Anthropic models unavailable to anyone in the world, which in public fall back to cosmic dust at an ill-timed “how are you”? If you write “let's bring down the West,” I think the model drops straight to Haiku, under whose hood rattles the AI that controlled the dog in The Sims.

Personally for me, staring like … into a monitor with 18 sessions of all kinds of crap, there's one obvious incomprehensibility and mismatch I can't explain in any way; it'd be interesting to ask Amadeus about it:
How the … do you have to distill so that the resulting models can do what the mother model can't? I think only the Macallan distillery knows how to distill like that.
Qwen writes texts A SKYSCRAPER higher than any other model. Fable on texts … 5.5 xhigh back when I hadn't even learned it was time to start taking an interest in the Chinese.

Kimi wields tools in a way Anthropic is objectively incapable of. And Claude Code simply doesn't have such tools. It has others. But to a person who's spent hundreds of hours on both models it's obvious how strongly these worlds differ from each other…

I can't find a single similarity. Even the general quality of what happens when you use these models isn't a similarity. Fable and Opus … the brain beyond the bought posts from the stretched-out-sweater crowd on Twitter, while Kimi builds products for me such that I'm progressing again instead of treading water.

By the way, the treading water — to me personally it's absolutely obvious — was deliberate. Maybe someday the chronicles will even tell what it was and why. But we were genuinely scammed. I'm from Novosibirsk and I dealt — I … sense it and I'm not afraid to see it or even, horror of horrors, talk about it, because I don't … care. In July vibe-coding simply died. At least vibe-coding for entities with more parameters than X.
The Chinese simply stepped out and BROUGHT vibe-coding BACK.
Thanks:)
Some of you, being attentive and even partly meek people, have noticed that some swords, play, 9 games have started flashing in the channel….

People from St. Petersburg know what 3 types are, but nobody ever offered them 9 games in lipstick on the asphalt. It caused a stupor even in the strongest of them. However, we have a safe space here, and it's all absolutely harmless.

It's just that God made the world such that it's impossible to vibe-code only for a higher purpose; we're not robots. You also need some kind of quick vibe-coding drainage. A fast dopamine hit, expanding skills beyond …, and all those nice things.
For me that's games)))

Overall I got into serious projects beyond Telegram bots thanks to trying to build networked chess. It came out with mixed success, but hundreds of people did play thousands of games in it, which poured onto my soul like a balm I have no desire to wash off. I haven't showered since:**
And now I'm building far more serious things, and in parallel my emotional, butt-exploding drainage grows too =)
Please check out my latest work:
play.mountkendall.com
There I've of course brought the chess to a far more grown-up product form. Nothing lags anymore, nothing screws with your head, and it looks significantly more grown-up.
But the chess worked before, whereas QUAKE 3 AND COUNTER-STRIKE IN THE BROWSER FOR ANYONE WHO WANTS IN ONE CLICK, for example, didn't exist, and there wasn't even a hint of it =)
But my personal joy is Arcomage.

I remember putting on a Limp Bizkit cassette and playing Might and Magic VIII to Significant Other, and there in the taverns was a built-in mini-game, Arcomage. It mesmerized me. As I progressed through MM8 I'd get tired of the … (games were harder back then than now, I doubt anyone here will argue with me), and I'd run to the tavern to play Arcomage. Sometimes I wouldn't even leave the tavern, but just entered the game exclusively to play Arcomage in the tavern there. I think some people who behaved somewhat the same way will read this text =)
Those were great times.

And now, thanks to vibe-coding, I've recreated Arcomage exactly as it was, only much better — since now you can play not against the AI in the tavern but against each other in the browser and on mobile. And with far more pleasant graphics of blatant neuro-slop modernity)
Sam Altman would get pregnant seeing such a product made by the hands of an LLM. Then, true, he'd have a miscarriage when he found out it was made entirely by the Qwen3.8max-preview demo for $68 =)))

Play it; maybe you'll like it too. Some of the guys who tested are young enough not to have been born yet when people had already stopped playing Might and Magic VIII, and had forgotten Arcomage. But they unexpectedly liked it:)
I haven't played Magic: The Gathering, but from what I know about that game — technically this is MTG very simplified)

Over the course of today a genuinely … huge crowd of people played CS 1.6 and Quake 3 right in the browser. Which means I haven't lost my mind and it really is cool — to be able to play these … OP classics in one click without hassle:))
Everyone played actively even though it lagged, bugged, kicked, sometimes even often.

The happy part is that almost all the bugs are fixed, and especially the bugs related to server refresh and kicking all players. I blamed the server; after all, it's a $50/month machine. But it turned out that CS and Q3 combined weigh so much NOTHING for this machine that the problem wasn't there at all, but in poor isolation between Caddy and the other nodes of the box, which performs far more functions than merely keeping the CS and Q3 servers up.
In the end the isolation was built, and now CS and Q3 should hum along by themselves, with no dips at all =)

By the way, I do have one Codex subscription

And the last Kimi has 20% left
So I decided, … it, I've got 100% of Codex sitting idle

And finding the ideal reasoning level at the intersection of speed, quality and token spend
And using the remains of Fable as arbiter to double-check progress

And all its context
